title: Fix support for embeddings generated by Ollama.
body: The existing code appears to assume that generated text embeddings for local search are normalized. However, it seems like Ollama violates this assumption. This causes incorrect behavior when using Ollama embeddings where every single query to the vector database will produce zero valid results. To fix this, I used a Langchain feature that can normalize embedding vectors automatically.

title: Add Serp API support in addition to DuckDuckGo
body:
# Add SerpAPI Integration Alongside DuckDuckGo for Search Expansion

## Summary
This PR enhances the existing search functionality by adding SerpAPI support in addition to DuckDuckGo, allowing users to switch between search providers dynamically. The implementation enables:

- The use of Google search via SerpAPI.
- The ability to select the search provider (DuckDuckGo or SerpAPI) using a configurable variable.
- Support for language-specific searches using a language mapping.
- Ensured compatibility with snippet-only search mode and full search results.

---

## Changes & Enhancements

### 1. Updated `config.py` to Support SerpAPI
- Added SerpAPI support alongside DuckDuckGo.
- Introduced a search provider selection variable (`search_tool`) to choose between `"serp"` (SerpAPI) and `"duckduckgo"`. 
- Implemented Google language codes mapping (`LANGUAGE_CODE_MAPPING`) to support multi-language searches.

### 2. Modified `get_search()` to Dynamically Use the Chosen Search Provider
- Uses `FullSerpAPISearchResults` when `search_tool = "serp"`, mirroring the existing `FullDuckDuckGoSearchResults`.
- Updated search parameters (safe search, language, time filters) to support SerpAPI.

### 3. Created a New File: `full_serp_search_results.py`
- Defines `FullSerpAPISearchResults`, similar to `FullDuckDuckGoSearchResults`.
- Utilizes SerpAPI to fetch full search results with proper integration into the existing system.

---
## Installation Requirement
- Before using SerpAPI, install the required package by running:
  ```bash
  pip install google-search-results

## Important Notes
- Ensure that the **`SERP_API_KEY`** is set as an environment variable before using SerpAPI.
- SerpAPI requires an active subscription; make sure there are enough **credits** to avoid query limits or failures (100 searches/month are available in the Free Plan).
